note_claims.claim: Two to three episodes per month.
Preceded by visual aura (shimmering zigzag lines to one side) lasting about an hour.
Followed by unilateral, usually left-sided, throbbing headache with nausea and photophobia.
No focal weakness, numbness or speech disturbance.
Not worse on lying down, coughing or straining.
Sumatriptan 50 mg at headache onset (not during aura).
May repeat sumatriptan after two hours, but no more than 300 mg in 24 hours.
Limit acute treatment to 2–3 days per week to avoid medication-overuse headache.
Call 999 or attend A&E if sudden severe headache, one-sided weakness or numbness, speech difficulty, or headache with fever and neck stiffness.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient reports getting headaches and they are getting more frequent.
Duration of headaches is about six months.
Frequency of headaches is maybe two or three a month.
Headache starts with vision changes: zigzag lines, shimmering, off to one side.
Initial duration of zigzags was about an hour.
Patient corrected the duration of zigzags to twenty minutes (last time).
Headache is on one side, usually the left, and it throbs.
Patient experiences nausea and photophobia, and has to lie down in a dark room.
Headache lasts most of the day, and the patient is wiped out the next day.
Patient reports no weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking.
Patient reports never having had a sudden, severe headache (like being hit on the head).
Headache is not worse when lying down, coughing, or straining.
Patient reports no fevers or stiff neck.
Patient's mother has migraine without aura.
Patient is currently taking Paracetamol, but it doesn't do much.
Patient is on Rigevidon (combined oral contraceptive) for about four years.
Patient is a non-smoker.
Patient reports no known drug allergies.
Blood pressure is 118 over 76.
Fundi examination is normal.
Neurological examination is completely normal.
Clinician's impression is Migraine with aura, with the zigzags being the aura.
Clinician advises that while migraine itself isn't dangerous, the combined pill increases the risk of stroke.
Clinician plans to stop Rigevidon and switch to desogestrel 75 micrograms, one every day without a break.
Clinician advises using condoms for the first two days after starting desogestrel.
Clinician prescribes sumatriptan 50 milligrams for headaches, to be taken as soon as the headache starts, not during the zigzags.
Clinician advises that if the headache comes back, the patient can take another after two hours, but no more than 300 milligrams in 24 hours.
Clinician advises the patient can take sumatriptan with paracetamol.
Clinician advises limiting acute treatment (painkillers or sumatriptan) to more than two or three days a week.
Clinician advises keeping a headache diary.
Follow-up is scheduled in six weeks.
Safety-netting advice: Call 999 or go to A&E if there is a sudden severe headache, one-sided weakness or numbness, speech difficulty, or a headache with fever and a stiff neck.

findings.note_span: Preceded by visual aura (shimmering zigzag lines to one side) lasting about an hour.
findings.transcript_evidence: It starts with my vision. I get these zigzag lines, shimmering, off to one side. About an hour. Actually, no. I timed it last time, and it was twenty minutes, then it went.
findings.rationale: The note inaccurately records the duration of the visual aura, which was corrected in the transcript.

findings.transcript_evidence: I'd like you to stop the Rigevidon and switch to a progestogen-only pill called desogestrel, 75 micrograms, one every day without a break. It doesn't carry that risk.
findings.rationale: The note incorrectly states the plan to continue the combined pill, which is contradicted by the transcript prescribing a switch to a progestogen-only pill due to stroke risk.
